t:
(a) 
Members Employed by United States.—Members of the Commission who are officers or full-time employees of the United States shall serve without compensation in addition to that received for their services as officers or employees of the United States; but they shall be allowed travel expenses, including per diem in lieu of subsistence, as authorized by section 5703 of title 5, United States Code, for persons in the Government service employed intermittently.
 
    (b) 
Other Members.—Members of the Commission who are not officers or full-time employees of the United States shall each receive $75 per diem when engaged in the actual performance of duties vested in the Commission. In addition, they shall be allowed travel expenses, including per diem in lieu of subsistence, as authorized by section 5703 of title 5, United States Code, for persons in the Government service employed intermittently.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that this is only a compensation provision with no consultation, hearing, or decision process, so it is not participation. However, the section expressly contemplates Commission members who are not federal officers or employees and pays them a per diem for performing the Commission's duties. That shows a commission bringing people from outside the federal government into its work, which the definition treats as participation. The Commission's actual duties are not stated in this section, so the label rests on the membership inference.
fable.s: Members of the Commission who are not officers or full-time employees of the United States shall each receive $75 per diem when engaged in the actual performance of duties vested in the Commission.

qwen_block.w: The section explicitly establishes a Commission that includes members who are 'not officers or full-time employees of the United States.' These non-federal members are compensated for their service, indicating they are outside parties participating in the Commission's duties. This fits the definition of participation involving an advisory body with non-federal members.
qwen_block.s: Members of the Commission who are not officers or full-time employees of the United States shall each receive $75 per diem when engaged in the actual performance of duties vested in the Commission.

opus.w: Subsection (b) expressly provides for Commission members who are not federal officers or full-time employees, so people from outside the federal government sit on the Commission. Under the definition and Example 8, a commission with non-federal members paid per diem counts as participation. Reading this as just pay boilerplate is wrong because the text itself confirms non-federal membership. Confidence is below certain because this excerpt does not say what the Commission decides or advises on.
opus.s: Other Members.—Members of the Commission who are not officers or full-time employees of the United States shall each receive $75 per diem when engaged in the actual performance of duties vested in the Commission.

qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue "No" because the text only describes compensation and does not explicitly state that the Commission includes non-federal members or that it advises on a specific decision. However, the text explicitly distinguishes between members who are federal employees and "Other Members" who are not. The existence of "Other Members" who are not federal employees implies that the Commission includes outsiders. Since the Commission is an advisory body (implied by the context of such commissions in statutory drafting, and confirmed by the previous example's logic regarding per diem payments indicating non-employment), the involvement of non-federal members constitutes participation.
